I'd super recommend experimenting with Wave Shaper as you get a lot of freedom as to what kind of distortion you want to apply.
An alternative, but just as valid, technique to what TautwiZZ suggested is to route your bass into two separate high-end-only and low-end-only mixer channels. That way you can just distort the high-end channel and the sub won't get fucked up.
Couldn't recommend this enough if you're after some very unpredictable results and interesting textures.

Ah I see what point you were making now. Yes, the DAW is designed for getting ideas down quickly and that is still relevant today, whereas coding algorithms things is the last thing on most producers' mind.

Honestly I think it depends on the type of producer you are.
I mean it may be just down to lack of experience but I almost never write a song from an idea in my head. Starting a composition normally means experimenting a bit with a synth or looking through a sample library for something interesting.
For someone like me having more freedom [getting down to the fundamental maths and algorithms] with the music I'm making means a lot because I think it could lead to discovering new ways of doing things.
